angle: Most agent tools demo well and collapse on a real task
hook: I ran 6 free AI agent tools on one real task
caption:
Agent demos are edited. I gave six free agent tools the same unglamorous job — read a folder of documents, pull out the numbers, and put them in a spreadsheet — and watched what happened. Two finished. The others looped, hallucinated a column, or stopped halfway and declared success.

💬 Comment "AGENTS" and I'll send you the full list.
🔖 Save this for the next time you need it.
➡️ Follow @profit_prompts_ for the AI stack that actually pays.

#aiagents #automation #aitools #productivity #freetools #workflow

slides.text: I ran 6 *free* AI agent tools on one real task
slides.subline: Two finished it. The rest looped or quit

slides.text: Every agent demo is a task chosen because it works. Give them your actual work and the field thins fast.

slides.title: Test with a boring job
slides.body: Do not test an agent on something impressive. Test it on the dull repetitive task you actually want gone. That is where the failures show up.

slides.caption: free agent tools that finished an ordinary real-world task

slides.title: Watch for the fake finish
slides.body: The most common failure is not a crash. It is an agent that stops early and reports success. Always check the output against the source yourself the first few runs.

slides.title: Keep the loop short
slides.body: Agents degrade the longer they run unsupervised. Give one a task it can finish in a few steps, check it, then chain another. Long autonomous runs are where the money and the accuracy both go.
